messages:
maria chen: FYI Emerald's dedicated pool started showing tail regressions after yesterday's kernel selector update. p95 for 512-token generation jumped ~2x (210ms -> 430ms) and p99 is worse. Filing here before paging oncall. :cry:

samir patel: Ugh. Do we have a repro SLA workload? sequence length distribution?

maria chen: Yes — their qps is low but sequences are long; median ~320 tokens, 95th ~780. We saw the shift after kernel-chooser started preferring the fused attention kernel for xsmm paths. Flamegraph attached: https://perf.internal/redwood/emerald/1956789012/flame.svg :eyes:

jia wong: That fused kernel has worse latency with large KV cache churn and large batch formation windows. I suspect continuous batching heuristics are grouping too many mid-sized requests because token_budget target is high.

tom harrison: Can you share the current dedicated batching config for Emerald?

maria chen: Current config (from dedicated config store):
```json
{"queue_policy": "token_budget", "max_queue_tokens": 20000, "token_budget_per_batch": 1200, "batch_formation_timeout_ms": 12, "kv_prefetch": "on"}
```

maria chen: Note: token_budget_per_batch is effectively allowing big batches to form. With long sequences, the fused kernel thrashes the KV cache and the runtime ends up with serialization points. Profiling shows large stall time in KV cache sync and kernel launch overhead.

samir patel: Hmm. Quick mitigations we could try: 1) lower token_budget_per_batch 2) increase batch_formation_timeout to let batching stabilize 3) enable kernel fallback for >512 tokens 4) soften kv_prefetch (disabled or async).

jia wong: Agreed. My recommended staged plan:
- Stage A (quick canary): token_budget_per_batch -> 800, max_queue_tokens -> 12000, batch_formation_timeout_ms -> 20, kv_prefetch -> async
- Stage B (if A helps): token_budget_per_batch -> 600, batch_formation_timeout_ms -> 30, enable kernel_fallback_threshold_tokens=512 so long sequences use the older stable kernel.

maria chen: I ran a micro-sim with the canary params locally. Command: `./tools/run_batch_sim --customer emerald --profile --q 12000 --tb 800 --timeout 20 --kv async` Results: p95 drop from 430ms -> 260ms, p99 from 980ms -> 420ms in the sim. Not perfect but big improvement.

tom harrison: Nice. Any regression risk to other customers from changing policies on the dedicated pool? Emerald is on a tenant-isolated pool, so config change is per-customer and safe. We should still roll canary to a single node first.

samir patel: I'll prepare the canary patch. Proposed config payload:
```json
{"queue_policy":"smoothing","max_queue_tokens":"12000","token_budget_per_batch":"800","batch_formation_timeout_ms":"20","kv_prefetch":"async","kernel_fallback_threshold_tokens":"512"}
```

jia wong: Also add a short-circuit to prefer the older kernel when the effective batch token count > 9000 — the fused kernel seems to win only in mid-sized batches. That prevents accidental worse-case.

maria chen: Agreed. I've got a small regression test set from Emerald (10k requests sampled) we can run against the canary nodes. I'll upload results post-deploy.

infra-bot: deploy requested by samir patel: patch/runtime/emerald-batching-canary -> canary-node-03. CI passed. ETA 2m.

samir patel: Rolling to canary-node-03 now. Watching traces and cost counters.

(5m later)

infra-bot: deploy complete: canary-node-03 applied patch/runtime/emerald-batching-canary.

maria chen: First 5k requests: p95 270ms, p99 460ms. KV stall time down ~45% in flamegraphs. :thumbsup:

jia wong: Good sign. Any change in throughput?

maria chen: Throughput steady; small increase in token/sec due to fewer stalls. CPU/GPU utilization on canary node unchanged.

tom harrison: Let's hold 30m for monitoring. If stable, promote to pool. Samir, can you prepare a follow-up to stage B for tomorrow running during low traffic window?

samir patel: Yep, scheduled for 05:00 UTC tomorrow. I'll also add telemetry to surface kernel selection counts and kv_prefetch evictions per minute.

maria chen: Thanks all. Filed a short incident note for Emerald support: https://track.internal/tickets/EM-3129 so CS is looped.

jia wong: One more note for runtime: we should tune the kernel selector cost model to include KV eviction penalty for large sequences. I can open a PR with the perf numbers.

samir patel: please do. Closing this thread for now, will update after stage B. :wave:
